chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, he said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abu al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Salih ibn 'Uqbah, from Bashir al-Dahhan.

He said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Sometimes I miss the Hajj, so I observe Arafa at the grave of al-Husayn. He said: Well done, O Bashir! Any believer who comes to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him), cognizant of his right, on a day other than Eid, twenty Hajj and twenty 'Umra, approved and accepted, and twenty expeditions alongside a sent prophet or a just Imam are written for him. And whoever comes to it on the day of Eid, a hundred Hajj and a hundred 'Umra and a hundred expeditions alongside a sent prophet or a just Imam are written for him. And whoever comes to it on the Day of Arafa, cognizant of his right, a thousand Hajj and a thousand 'Umra, approved and accepted, and a thousand expeditions alongside a sent prophet or a just Imam are written for him.

He said: Then I said to him: And how can I have the like of the standing place [at Arafat]? He said: He looked at me like one angered, then said: O Bashir! Indeed, when the believer comes to the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) on the Day of Arafa and washes in the Euphrates, then heads toward it, God, Mighty and Majestic, writes for him with every step a Hajj with its rituals — and I do not know it except that he said: and an expedition.

key_terms.الموقف: The standing place — reference to the ritual standing (wuquf) at Arafat during Hajj
key_terms.زيارة: Ziyarat — pilgrimage visit to the shrine of an Imam or saint
key_terms.عرفة: Arafa — the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah, when Hajj pilgrims stand at the plain of Arafat; also observed at Imam Husayn's grave
key_terms.مبرورات متقبلات: Approved and accepted — indicating that the reward is a complete, divinely accepted act of worship

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for visiting the grave of Imam Husayn on the Day of Arafa?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Amali of al-Shaykh al-Saduq records Bashir al-Dahhan's conversation with Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the immense spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (AS). The Imam describes an escalating scale of rewards: twenty Hajj on ordinary days, a hundred on Eid, and a thousand on the Day of Arafa. When Bashir asks whether this compares to the standing at Arafat itself, the Imam emphasizes that the believer who bathes in the Euphrates and walks toward the shrine on the Day of Arafa earns a Hajj with every step. This teaching reflects the central importance of the ziyarat of Imam Husayn (AS) in Shia devotional practice, particularly in the context of pilgrims who could not make the journey to Mecca.
